newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS BEATS WASHINGTON, CHIEFS SNEAK BY LIONS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS BEATS WASHINGTON, CHIEFS SNEAK BY LIONS.

text.p: Emmitt Smith bounced back from one of the worst games of his career by rushing for 155 yards and three touchdowns as the Dallas Cowboys beat the Washington Redskins 21-10 on Thursday.

Smith, who was held to 18 yards on 11 carries in Sunday's 20-6 loss to the New York Giants, did not practice Monday or Tuesday and his status for this game was questionable. But he started and showed no signs of his ankle injury, carrying 29 times and scoring all three Dallas touchdowns.

"I hope this puts to rest the question of what Emmitt can do," Cowboys coach Barry Switzer said. "I talked with Emmitt and we knew it would be a game-day decision. After warmups, we talked to him and he said he felt better than he had in a while. He said we would know after just a few plays whether he could do it."

Smith went in from the 4-yard line late in the second quarter to open the scoring, put the Cowboys ahead to stay with another four-yard touchdown in the third and added an insurance TD midway through the fourth.
"I ran the ball the best I've run it all year long," he said. "The rest this week and the treatment all worked to let me have a little spring in my step and do some cutting and slashing."

Troy Aikman completed only 9-of-19 passes for 63 yards -- his lowest total since he had 29 yards before leaving with a bruised left knee against San Francisco on November 12th, 1995. But Dallas (8-5) won for the seventh time in nine games.
Gus Frerotte struggled for the Redskins, going 17-for-33 for 175 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Washington (8-5) has lost four of its last five games.

Smith eclipsed the 1,000-yard mark for the sixth straight season and topped the 100-yard mark for the sixth time in his career against Washington. The Redskins had not allowed him to gain 100 yards since December 26th, 1993.
The Cowboys held Terry Allen, the NFC rushing leader, to a season-low 34 yards on 12 carries.
In Detroit, Marcus Allen rushed for 73 yards and two touchdowns, including a one-yard scoring dive with 46 seconds left to lift the Kansas City Chiefs to a 28-24 victory over the Detroit Lions.

After Jason Hanson's 21-yard field goal gave the Lions (5-8) a 24-21 lead with 8:41 to play, Kansas City (9-4) embarked on a 15-play, 76-yard drive that consumed nearly eight minutes. Greg Hill, who totalled 103 yards on 17 carries, had 37 yards in the decisive series that led to Allen's score.

Allen, who handled the ball 15 times, broke a tie with Walter Payton (110) and became the NFL's all-time rushing touchdowns leader 11:11 into the game with a one-yard TD plunge. The Chiefs outrushed Detroit, 243-81.
"Breaking or borrowing the record, it couldn't have come on a better day," said Allen. "I'm appreciative of the guys around me here and in Oakland. We were confident coming in during the whole week."

Kansas City quarterback Rich Gannon, starting for the first time since 1993, completed 15-of-18 passes for 120 yards and two touchdowns. He had made his first appearance of the year last week when he replaced an ineffective Steve Bono late in the third quarter of a 28-14 loss to San Diego.

"It certainly wasn't pretty, but we got the job done," said Gannon. "I'm trying to work my way through it. I haven't played in a while. I felt like I got off some things a little bit early. If I'd gone out and stunk the place up, I could always say I'm the number two guy. Not that I would, but that's always in my back pocket."

The Chiefs have won four of their last five games and crept within 2-1/2 games of Denver for first place in the AFC West. Kansas City has won five of eight career meetings with Detroit and won on Thanksgiving for the second straight year.
